'''Lower Angara''' is a region of Russia. It is seen as a link between [[Northern Siberia]] and [[Southern Siberia]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Malov |first1=V.Iu |last2=Tarasova |first2=O.V. |last3=Ionova |first3=V.D. |date=2020-09-01 |title=The Lower Angara as a Link Between Northern and Southern Siberia |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10611991.2020.2033505 |journal=Problems of Economic Transition |language=en |volume=62 |issue=7–9 |pages=441–458 |doi=10.1080/10611991.2020.2033505 |s2cid=248157706 |issn=1061-1991|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It corresponds to the lower regions of the [[Angara River]]

Lower Angara is one of two rivers of Asiatic Russia, in the government of Irkutsk. it rises in the mountains to the east of Lake Baikal, and falls into the head of Lake Baikal after flowing nearly 300 miles. The current of the river is very strong, forming several rapids in its progress. The scenery on its banks is frequently extremely beautiful.<ref>{{EB9 |wstitle= Upper and Lower Angara |volume= II |page=26 |short= 1}}</ref>

The area has notable rock art<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zaika |first=A. L. |date=2012-03-01 |title=Face images in Lower Angara rock art |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1563011012000384 |journal=Archaeology, Ethnology and Anthropology of Eurasia |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=62–75 |doi=10.1016/j.aeae.2012.05.008 |issn=1563-0110|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and is a major carbon sink although fires have weakened it.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ivanova |first1=G. A. |last2=Conard |first2=S. G. |last3=Kukavskaya |first3=E. A. |last4=McRae |first4=D. J. |date=October 2011 |title=Fire impact on carbon storage in light conifer forests of the Lower Angara region, Siberia |journal=Environmental Research Letters |language=en |volume=6 |issue=4 |article-number=045203 |doi=10.1088/1748-9326/6/4/045203 |bibcode=2011ERL.....6d5203I |s2cid=154993661 |issn=1748-9326|doi-access=free }}</ref>
